column1: # Most specific match: the pattern with the most matching key/value pairs
# wins, wherever its keys come in the alphabet. Patterns with equally many
# pairs are ranked by their keys in alphabetical order.
# A longer pattern beats a shorter pattern on an earlier key
# The order of insertion makes no difference
# Equally many pairs: the keys in alphabetical order decide
# Three pairs beat two, and two beat one
# A later branch is still tried when an earlier one runs out
# A catch-all root pattern does not hide a more specific match
# Many overlapping patterns: the longest match wins
# Exact find needs one pattern to match every key
# Collect still returns every match, widest first along each branch
# A key that the subject does not have never matches
# gex: a missing key does not match a glob
# gex: a glob is still tried when the exact value leads nowhere
# gex: more pairs still win, whether matched exactly or by glob
# gex: with equally many pairs an exact value beats a glob
# gex: collect returns the glob matches as well as the exact one
